subject: Full Test
topic: Full syllabus — all subjects A-E (exam simulation)

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct option to complete the sentence: The committee has still not arrived ______ a decision on the matter.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'arrive at a decision', so 'at' is correct. 'Arrive on' is used with dates or occasions, 'arrive to' is not standard with 'decision', and 'arrive in' is used with large places like a country or city, so none of those fits with 'decision'.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct article: There is ______ university in our town that is famous for law.
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with the consonant sound /j/ ('yoo'), so it takes 'a', not 'an'. 'An' is used only before a vowel sound, which 'university' does not have. 'The' would point to a specific university already known, and omitting the article is wrong for a singular countable noun being introduced, so 'a' is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank with the correct word: The two friends confided ______ each other and shared all their secrets.
questions.explanation: 'Confide in someone' means to trust them with secrets, so 'in' is correct. 'Confide to' is used with the secret itself, not the person, while 'confide on' and 'confide with' are not standard collocations, so 'in' is the right preposition here.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to 'TENACIOUS'.
questions.explanation: 'Tenacious' means holding firmly to a purpose, so 'persistent' is the closest synonym. 'Fragile' means easily broken, the opposite of a firm grip. 'Careless' means lacking attention, and 'generous' means giving freely, neither of which relates to determined persistence.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the antonym of the word 'GENEROUS'.
questions.explanation: 'Generous' means willing to give freely, so its antonym is 'stingy' (unwilling to spend or give). 'Kind', 'liberal' and 'charitable' are all close in meaning to generous rather than opposite, so 'stingy' is the correct antonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following sentences:

(i) The scenery here are very beautiful.
(ii) He gave me an important information.
(iii) The furniture in the office is new.
(iv) She bought two dozen bananas.

Which of the sentences given above are grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun taking a singular verb, so (iii) is correct, and 'two dozen bananas' is correct usage, so (iv) is right. (i) is wrong because 'scenery' is uncountable and needs 'is', not 'are'. (ii) is wrong because 'information' is uncountable and cannot take 'an', so only (iii) and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct verb form: Unless you ______ immediately, you will miss the train.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' introduces a conditional clause that takes the simple present, so 'leave' is correct while the main clause uses 'will miss'. 'Will leave' wrongly puts the future in the conditional clause, 'left' is simple past, and 'had left' is past perfect, neither of which fits this first-conditional sentence.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Identify the correctly spelled word from the options below.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'occurrence', with double 'c', double 'r' and ending in '-ence'. 'Occurence' misses an 'r', 'Ocurrence' misses a 'c', and 'Occurrance' wrongly ends in '-ance', so 'Occurrence' is the correctly spelled word.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Identify the type of the underlined clause: I will help you because you are my friend.
questions.explanation: 'Because you are my friend' explains why the action happens, modifying the verb 'help', so it is an adverb clause of reason. It is not a noun clause (which acts as a subject or object), nor an adjective clause (which describes a noun), nor the main clause, since it depends on 'I will help you'.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly formed plural nouns?

(i) Leaves
(ii) Sheeps
(iii) Geese
(iv) Children

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: 'Leaves' (plural of leaf), 'geese' (plural of goose) and 'children' (plural of child) are all correct (i, iii, iv). 'Sheeps' (ii) is wrong because 'sheep' has the same form in singular and plural, so any option containing (ii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct pronoun: Everyone must submit ______ assignment before the deadline.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is grammatically singular, so the traditionally correct possessive is 'his or her'. 'Their' is a common informal plural usage but not the strictly correct singular form here. 'Theirs' is a possessive pronoun that cannot precede a noun, and 'them' is an object pronoun, so 'his or her' is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the idioms in Column I with their meanings in Column II:

Column I:
(a) A blessing in disguise
(b) To break the ice
(c) To burn one's fingers
(d) To keep one's word

Column II:
(i) To suffer a loss by involving oneself
(ii) To honour a promise
(iii) A good thing that seemed bad at first
(iv) To start a conversation in a tense situation

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 'A blessing in disguise' is a good thing that first seemed bad (iii); 'break the ice' means to start a conversation (iv); 'burn one's fingers' means to suffer a loss (i); 'keep one's word' means to honour a promise (ii). The other options swap 'blessing in disguise' with 'burn one's fingers' or misassign 'break the ice', which are incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To make a mountain out of a molehill'.
questions.explanation: 'To make a mountain out of a molehill' means to treat a trivial issue as if it were serious, i.e. to exaggerate. It does not mean achieving a feat, nor literally climbing, nor hiding a fact, so those options miss the idiom's meaning of overstating a small problem.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct option: Hardly had the train left the station ______ the passenger reached the platform.
questions.explanation: The structure 'Hardly had ... when ...' is the fixed correlative, so 'when' is correct. 'Than' pairs with 'no sooner', not 'hardly'; 'then' is an adverb of time, not a conjunction here; and 'that' does not complete the 'hardly ... when' structure, so 'when' is right.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank with the correct word: The scientist's discovery had a profound ______ on modern medicine.
questions.explanation: 'Effect' is a noun meaning result or influence, which fits 'a profound effect'. 'Affect' is normally a verb meaning to influence, so it does not fit after 'a profound'. 'Effort' means attempt, and 'aspect' means a feature, neither of which conveys influence, so 'effect' is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the option that best completes the analogy: 'Pen' is to 'Writer' as 'Brush' is to ______.
questions.explanation: A pen is the tool of a writer just as a brush is the tool of a painter, so the tool-to-user relationship holds. 'Canvas' is the surface a painter works on, 'colour' is the medium, and 'wall' is a possible surface, none of which is the user of the brush, so 'painter' is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following sentences about subject-verb agreement:

(i) Mathematics is my favourite subject.
(ii) The news are very disturbing.
(iii) Ten kilometres is a long distance to walk.
(iv) The scissors is on the table.

Which of the sentences given above are grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: 'Mathematics' takes a singular verb (i), and a measured distance like 'ten kilometres' is treated as a single unit taking 'is' (iii). (ii) is wrong because 'news' is uncountable and takes 'is', not 'are'. (iv) is wrong because 'scissors' is a plural-only noun taking 'are', so only (i) and (iii) are correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: Where are you going, she asked.
Where are you going? she asked.
questions.explanation: Direct speech must be enclosed in quotation marks with the question mark inside, so the second option is correct. The first omits quotation marks, the third wrongly uses a comma inside the quote and misplaces the question mark, and the fourth omits quotation marks entirely, so only the second is correctly punctuated.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive form of: 'The gardener waters the plants every morning.'
options: The plants were watered by the gardener every morning.
The plants are watered by the gardener every morning.
The plants have been watered by the gardener every morning.
The plants are being watered by the gardener every morning.
questions.correctAnswer: The plants are watered by the gardener every morning.
questions.explanation: The active sentence is in the simple present, so its passive is 'are watered'. 'Were watered' is simple past, 'have been watered' is present perfect, and 'are being watered' is present continuous, none of which matches the simple present habitual action, so 'are watered' is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Which of the following words are adverbs?

(i) Quickly
(ii) Happiness
(iii) Carefully
(iv) Silently

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: 'Quickly', 'carefully' and 'silently' describe how an action is done, so they are adverbs (i, iii, iv). 'Happiness' (ii) is an abstract noun naming a feeling, not an adverb, so any option containing (ii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the word most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to 'AMIABLE'.
questions.explanation: 'Amiable' means having a pleasant, friendly manner, so 'friendly' is the closest synonym. 'Hostile' is its opposite, meaning unfriendly. 'Clever' refers to intelligence and 'wealthy' to riches, neither of which relates to a warm disposition, so 'friendly' is correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Match the words in Column I with the parts of speech in Column II as used generally:

Column I:
(a) Beautiful
(b) Run
(c) Quickly
(d) Under

Column II:
(i) Verb
(ii) Preposition
(iii) Adjective
(iv) Adverb

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 'Beautiful' describes a noun, so it is an adjective (iii); 'run' is an action, a verb (i); 'quickly' describes how, an adverb (iv); 'under' shows position, a preposition (ii). The other options wrongly label 'beautiful' as a verb or swap 'quickly' and 'under', which misidentifies the parts of speech.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Select the antonym of the word 'ANCIENT'.
questions.explanation: 'Ancient' means belonging to the very distant past, so its antonym is 'modern' (of the present or recent times). 'Old', 'antique' and 'aged' are similar in meaning to ancient rather than opposite, so 'modern' is the correct antonym.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText:
Consider the following sentences:

(i) He returned back home after the meeting.
(ii) She is one of the best singers in the choir.
(iii) The reason for his failure is because he was lazy.
(iv) I look forward to meeting you soon.

Which of the sentences given above are grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: 'One of the best singers' (ii) and 'look forward to meeting' (iv) are correct. (i) is wrong because 'returned back' is redundant; 'returned home' suffices. (iii) is wrong because 'the reason ... is because' is redundant; it should be 'the reason ... is that', so only (ii) and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: A
questions.questionText: Choose the correct question tag: She rarely comes late to office, ______?
questions.explanation: The adverb 'rarely' gives the sentence a negative sense, so the tag must be positive: 'does she'. 'Doesn't she' wrongly adds a second negative, and 'is she'/'isn't she' use the wrong auxiliary (the verb is 'comes', needing 'do'), so 'does she' is the correct tag.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Champaran Satyagraha' of 1917, led by Mahatma Gandhi, was related to the grievances of which group?
questions.explanation: The Champaran Satyagraha in Bihar addressed the exploitation of indigo cultivators forced to grow indigo under the tinkathia system. Textile workers were involved in the Ahmedabad mill strike, salt makers in the Salt Satyagraha, and railway employees in other movements, so indigo cultivators is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian geography:

(i) The Thar Desert lies mainly in Rajasthan.
(ii) The Nilgiri Hills are a part of the Himalayan range.
(iii) The Ganga originates from the Gangotri glacier.
(iv) The Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Thar Desert is mainly in Rajasthan (i), the Ganga rises from the Gangotri glacier (iii), and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal (iv). Statement (ii) is wrong because the Nilgiri Hills belong to the Western Ghats, not the Himalayas, so any option containing (ii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Himalayas protect India from cold Central Asian winds.
Reason (R): The Himalayas are the youngest and highest mountain ranges in the world.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The Himalayas do act as a barrier to cold northern winds, so (A) is correct, and they are indeed among the youngest and highest ranges, so (R) is correct. However, their protective role is due to their height and position as a barrier, not merely to being young, so (R) does not fully explain (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first Indian to hold the office of Governor-General of India?
questions.explanation: C. Rajagopalachari was the first (and last) Indian Governor-General of India, succeeding Lord Mountbatten. Rajendra Prasad became the first President, Sardar Patel was Deputy Prime Minister, and Nehru was Prime Minister, so none of them held the Governor-General's office, making Rajagopalachari correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the languages officially recognised by the country?
questions.explanation: The Eighth Schedule lists the officially recognised (scheduled) languages of India. The Seventh Schedule contains the division of powers between the Union and states, the Ninth Schedule protects certain laws from judicial review, and the Sixth Schedule deals with tribal areas, so the Eighth Schedule is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's space programme:

(i) ISRO's headquarters is located in Bengaluru.
(ii) Chandrayaan-1 was India's first lunar mission.
(iii) The Mangalyaan mission was sent to Jupiter.
(iv) Aryabhata was India's first satellite.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: ISRO is headquartered in Bengaluru (i), Chandrayaan-1 was India's first lunar mission (ii), and Aryabhata was India's first satellite (iv). Statement (iii) is wrong because the Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission) was sent to Mars, not Jupiter, so any option with (iii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the national parks in Column I with the states in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Kaziranga
(b) Gir
(c) Jim Corbett
(d) Sundarbans

Column II:
(i) Uttarakhand
(ii) Assam
(iii) West Bengal
(iv) Gujarat

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Kaziranga is in Assam (ii), Gir in Gujarat (iv), Jim Corbett in Uttarakhand (i) and Sundarbans in West Bengal (iii). The other options swap Kaziranga's state or misplace Jim Corbett and Sundarbans, which are factually incorrect pairings.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are classified as Fundamental Rights under the Indian Constitution?

(i) Right to Equality
(ii) Right to Property
(iii) Right against Exploitation
(iv) Right to Freedom of Religion

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Right to Equality (i), the Right against Exploitation (iii) and the Right to Freedom of Religion (iv) are Fundamental Rights. The Right to Property (ii) was removed as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment and is now only a legal right, so any option containing (ii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which gas is released by green plants into the atmosphere during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: During photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen as a by-product. Carbon dioxide is absorbed, not released, nitrogen is not involved in this reaction, and hydrogen is not released as a gas, so oxygen is the correct answer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The ______ Sagar Dam, built on the Sutlej river, is one of the highest gravity dams in India.
questions.explanation: The Bhakra (Bhakra-Nangal) Dam on the Sutlej is one of India's highest gravity dams. The Hirakud Dam is on the Mahanadi, the Tehri Dam is on the Bhagirathi, and the Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is on the Krishna, so Bhakra is the dam on the Sutlej.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Nobel Prize' for outstanding contributions is awarded by institutions of which country (except the Peace Prize)?
questions.explanation: The Nobel Prizes in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature and Economics are awarded by Swedish institutions, following Alfred Nobel's will. Only the Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Norway. Switzerland and Denmark are not involved in awarding the prizes, so Sweden is correct for the science and literature prizes.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Read the following data on the literacy rate (in %) of four states:

State P → 96
State Q → 74
State R → 82
State S → 66

What is the difference between the highest and the lowest literacy rate?
questions.explanation: The highest literacy rate is 96 (State P) and the lowest is 66 (State S), so the difference is 96 − 66 = 30. 22 uses the wrong pair (96 − 74), 14 uses (96 − 82), and 34 is a miscalculation, so 30 is the correct difference.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian classical dance forms:

(i) Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu.
(ii) Kathakali is a dance form of Kerala.
(iii) Odissi belongs to the state of Odisha.
(iv) Kuchipudi originated in Punjab.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam is from Tamil Nadu (i), Kathakali from Kerala (ii), and Odissi from Odisha (iii). Statement (iv) is wrong because Kuchipudi originated in Andhra Pradesh, not Punjab, so any option containing (iv) is incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Rupiah' is the official currency of which country?
questions.explanation: The Rupiah is the currency of Indonesia. Malaysia uses the Ringgit, Thailand uses the Baht, and the Philippines uses the Peso, so none of those countries uses the Rupiah, making Indonesia correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The President of India is elected directly by the citizens.
Reason (R): The President is the head of the executive branch of the Union.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: (A) is false because the President is elected indirectly by an electoral college of elected MPs and MLAs, not directly by citizens. (R) is correct because the President is the constitutional head of the Union executive. Hence (A) is not correct but (R) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following is the southernmost point of mainland India?
questions.explanation: Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin) in Tamil Nadu is the southernmost tip of the Indian mainland. Indira Point is the southernmost point of Indian territory but lies in the Nicobar Islands, not the mainland. Rameswaram and Kochi lie further north, so Kanyakumari is correct for the mainland.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Rabi crops in India?

(i) Wheat
(ii) Mustard
(iii) Rice
(iv) Gram

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Wheat, mustard and gram are sown in winter and harvested in spring, so they are Rabi crops (i, ii, iv). Rice (iii) is a Kharif crop grown in the monsoon season, so any option containing (iii) is incorrect, leaving (i), (ii) and (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Ayushman Bharat' scheme launched by the Government of India is primarily related to which sector?
questions.explanation: Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) provides health insurance cover for hospitalisation to eligible families. Education is served by schemes like Samagra Shiksha, rural employment by MGNREGA, and housing by PM Awas Yojana, so Ayushman Bharat belongs to the health sector.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who among the following was the first woman President of India?
questions.explanation: Pratibha Patil became the first woman President of India in 2007. Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of an Indian state, while Sonia Gandhi and Sushma Swaraj were prominent politicians but never Presidents, so Pratibha Patil is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about famous Indian personalities and their fields:

(i) Homi J. Bhabha is called the father of India's nuclear programme.
(ii) M. S. Swaminathan is associated with the Green Revolution.
(iii) Verghese Kurien led the White Revolution.
(iv) Vikram Sarabhai is known as the father of the Indian textile industry.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Homi Bhabha is the father of India's nuclear programme (i), M. S. Swaminathan is linked to the Green Revolution (ii), and Verghese Kurien led the White Revolution in milk (iii). Statement (iv) is wrong because Vikram Sarabhai is regarded as the father of the Indian space programme, not the textile industry, so (iv) is excluded.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The IMF is headquartered in Washington D.C., USA, close to the World Bank. Geneva hosts bodies like the WHO, New York hosts the UN headquarters, and London is home to other institutions, so Washington D.C. is the correct location of the IMF.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'checkmate' is associated with which of the following games?
questions.explanation: 'Checkmate' is the winning move in chess where the opponent's king cannot escape capture. Carrom uses terms like 'striker' and 'queen', bridge uses 'trump' and 'bid', and Ludo uses dice, so none of them uses 'checkmate', making chess correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which is the most abundant metal found in the Earth's crust?
questions.explanation: Aluminium is the most abundant metal in the Earth's crust, followed by iron. Copper and calcium are present in smaller proportions, and though iron is the second most abundant metal, it is less than aluminium, so aluminium is the correct answer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Lok Sabha is more powerful than the Rajya Sabha in money matters.
Reason (R): A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The Lok Sabha does have greater power over money matters, so (A) is correct, and a Money Bill can indeed be introduced only in the Lok Sabha (not the Rajya Sabha), so (R) is correct. Because this exclusive power to introduce Money Bills is precisely what gives the Lok Sabha its financial dominance, (R) explains (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Jnanpith Award' in India is given for excellence in the field of:
questions.explanation: The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honour, given for outstanding contribution to literature. Science awards include the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize, sports honours include the Khel Ratna, and cinema is recognised by the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, so literature is the field for the Jnanpith Award.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Dogra dynasty that ruled Jammu and Kashmir until 1947 was founded by which ruler?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Gulab Singh founded the Dogra dynasty after acquiring the region under the Treaty of Amritsar in 1846. Ranjit Singh was the Sikh ruler of Punjab, while Hari Singh and Pratap Singh were later Dogra rulers, so Gulab Singh is the founder of the dynasty.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Betaab Valley, a popular tourist spot named after a Hindi film, is located near which town?
questions.explanation: The Betaab Valley lies near Pahalgam in the Anantnag district and was named after the film shot there. Gulmarg and Sonamarg are separate destinations, and Kokernag is known for its springs and gardens, so Pahalgam is the town near the Betaab Valley.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Jammu and Kashmir:

(i) Kokernag is famous for its freshwater springs.
(ii) Verinag is regarded as the source of the Jhelum river.
(iii) Yusmarg is located in the Budgam district.
(iv) The Dal Lake is located in the Jammu region.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Kokernag is famous for its springs (i), Verinag is the source of the Jhelum (ii), and Yusmarg is in Budgam (iii). Statement (iv) is wrong because the Dal Lake is in Srinagar in the Kashmir valley, not in the Jammu region, so any option with (iv) is incorrect.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Pashmina wool is obtained from a special breed of goat reared in the higher reaches of the region.
Reason (R): The cold, high-altitude climate helps the goats grow fine, soft undercoats.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Pashmina is obtained from Changthangi goats reared at high altitudes, so (A) is correct, and the cold high-altitude climate causes these goats to grow a fine, soft undercoat, so (R) is correct. Since the climate is precisely what produces the fine wool, (R) correctly explains (A).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The famous Tulip Garden, one of the largest in Asia, is situated at the foothills of which range near Srinagar?
questions.explanation: The Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden lies on the foothills of the Zabarwan range beside the Dal Lake in Srinagar. The Pir Panjal separates the valley from Jammu, while the Karakoram and Zanskar ranges lie in the Ladakh region, so the Zabarwan range is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are districts of the Jammu division?

(i) Rajouri
(ii) Poonch
(iii) Kupwara
(iv) Kathua

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Rajouri, Poonch and Kathua all lie in the Jammu division (i, ii, iv). Kupwara (iii) is a district of the Kashmir valley in the far north, so any option containing (iii) is incorrect, leaving (i), (ii) and (iv).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ river is the largest river of Jammu and Kashmir by water volume and is dammed at several hydroelectric projects.
questions.explanation: The Chenab carries the largest volume of water among the region's rivers and hosts major projects like Baglihar, Salal and Dulhasti. The Jhelum drains the valley but carries less volume, the Tawi is a smaller Jammu river, and the Ravi flows along the southern border, so the Chenab is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Achabal and Kokernag gardens, laid out during the Mughal era, are located in which district of the Kashmir valley?
questions.explanation: Both the Achabal garden and the Kokernag springs and garden lie in the Anantnag district in the south of the valley. Srinagar has the Shalimar and Nishat gardens, while Baramulla and Ganderbal do not host Achabal and Kokernag, so Anantnag is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Jammu and Kashmir:

(i) The Jhelum is the main river of the Kashmir valley.
(ii) Srinagar is famous for its houseboats on the Dal Lake.
(iii) The Tawi river flows through the city of Srinagar.
(iv) Anantnag lies in the southern part of the Kashmir valley.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Jhelum is the main river of the valley (i), Srinagar is famous for houseboats on the Dal Lake (ii), and Anantnag lies in south Kashmir (iv). Statement (iii) is wrong because the Tawi flows through Jammu city, not Srinagar, so any option containing (iii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Gurez Valley, known for its scenic beauty and the Habba Khatoon peak, lies in which district?
questions.explanation: The Gurez Valley, along the Kishanganga river and overlooked by the pyramid-shaped Habba Khatoon peak, lies in the Bandipora district. Kupwara, Baramulla and Ganderbal are nearby districts but do not contain the Gurez Valley, so Bandipora is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A shopkeeper buys 12 pens for ₹100 and sells them at ₹10 each. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Cost price of 12 pens = ₹100; selling price = 12 × 10 = ₹120. Profit = ₹20 on ₹100, i.e. 20%. 15%, 25% and 18% do not equal the ratio of ₹20 profit to ₹100 cost, so 20% is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: In a code, 'LIGHT' is written as 'MJHIU'. Using the same rule, how is 'SOUND' written?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted one place forward: L→M, I→J, G→H, H→I, T→U. Applying this to SOUND: S→T, O→P, U→V, N→O, D→E, giving TPVOE. TPVOF mis-shifts D, TQVOE mis-shifts O, and TPWOE mis-shifts U, so TPVOE is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: The average weight of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person replaces one weighing 65 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation: The total weight increases by 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg, so the new person is 20 kg heavier than the one replaced: 65 + 20 = 85 kg. 80 kg, 90 kg and 75 kg do not match this 20 kg increase, so 85 kg is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Every square is a rectangle.
Reason (R): A square has four right angles and opposite sides equal, satisfying the definition of a rectangle.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: A square is a special rectangle, so (A) is correct, and a square does have four right angles with opposite sides equal, meeting the definition of a rectangle, so (R) is correct. Because satisfying the rectangle definition is exactly why a square is a rectangle, (R) correctly explains (A).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: The side of a square is increased by 20%. By what percentage does its area increase?
questions.explanation: If the side becomes 1.2 times the original, the area becomes (1.2)² = 1.44 times, i.e. a 44% increase. A 40% or 20% answer wrongly doubles or copies the side increase, and 21% is not the correct squared effect, so 44% is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A and B start from the same point. A walks 4 km north and B walks 3 km east. What is the shortest distance between them now?
questions.explanation: Their paths are perpendicular, so the distance between them is √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 km. 7 km simply adds the distances, while 6 km and 4 km do not satisfy the Pythagorean relation, so 5 km is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: Find the missing number in the series: 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, ______
questions.explanation: Each term is obtained by doubling the previous term and subtracting 1: 2×2−1=3, 3×2−1=5, 5×2−1=9, 9×2−1=17, so 17×2−1 = 33. 31, 34 and 35 do not follow the 'double and subtract one' rule, so 33 is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A swimmer covers 20 km downstream in 2 hours and the same 20 km upstream in 5 hours. What is the speed of the stream (current)?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 20/2 = 10 km/h; upstream speed = 20/5 = 4 km/h. Stream speed = (downstream − upstream)/2 = (10 − 4)/2 = 3 km/h. 2 km/h, 5 km/h and 4 km/h do not equal half the difference of the two speeds, so 3 km/h is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about basic numbers:

(i) The smallest two-digit number is 10.
(ii) The largest three-digit number is 999.
(iii) The smallest prime number is 2.
(iv) The smallest whole number is 1.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The smallest two-digit number is 10 (i), the largest three-digit number is 999 (ii), and the smallest prime is 2 (iii). Statement (iv) is wrong because the smallest whole number is 0, not 1, so any option containing (iv) is incorrect, leaving (i), (ii) and (iii).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: If 12 men can finish a task in 15 days, how many additional men are needed to finish the same task in 9 days?
questions.explanation: Total work = 12 × 15 = 180 man-days. To finish in 9 days, men needed = 180/9 = 20. Since 12 are already there, additional men = 20 − 12 = 8. Answering 20 gives the total not the extra; 6, 10 and 5 do not equal the additional requirement, so 8 is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Match the shapes in Column I with their number of sides in Column II:

Column I:
(a) Pentagon
(b) Octagon
(c) Hexagon
(d) Heptagon

Column II:
(i) 8
(ii) 5
(iii) 7
(iv) 6

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: A pentagon has 5 sides (ii), an octagon 8 (i), a hexagon 6 (iv) and a heptagon 7 (iii). The other options swap the octagon's and hexagon's sides or interchange the heptagon and hexagon, giving wrong side counts, so only the first mapping is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: Through how many degrees does the minute hand of a clock move in 20 minutes?
questions.explanation: The minute hand completes 360° in 60 minutes, i.e. 6° per minute. In 20 minutes it moves 20 × 6 = 120°. 90° would be 15 minutes, 60° would be 10 minutes, and 180° would be 30 minutes, so 120° is correct for 20 minutes.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: Two numbers whose sum is 20 have a product of 96. Find the positive difference between the two numbers.
questions.explanation: The two numbers with a sum of 20 and a product of 96 are 12 and 8, since 12 + 8 = 20 and 12 × 8 = 96. Their positive difference is 12 − 8 = 4. The values 6, 8 and 2 are not the difference of these numbers, so 4 is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: Simplify: 8 × (6 + 4) ÷ 5 - 3
questions.explanation: By BODMAS, brackets first: 6 + 4 = 10; then 8 × 10 = 80; then 80 ÷ 5 = 16; then 16 − 3 = 13. Ignoring the bracket or the order of operations gives 16, 11 or 9, so 13 is the correct value.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A certain sum becomes ₹4,410 in 2 years at 5% per annum compound interest. What was the original sum?

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: Which letter-cluster should replace the question mark? AB, DE, GH, JK, ?
questions.explanation: Each pair skips one letter after it: AB (skip C) DE (skip F) GH (skip I) JK (skip L) MN. So the next pair is MN. LM starts one letter too early, MO breaks the consecutive pattern, and NO skips ahead, so MN is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The number 17 is a prime number.
Reason (R): A prime number has exactly two distinct factors, 1 and itself.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: 17 has only the factors 1 and 17, so it is prime and (A) is correct. (R) correctly defines a prime number as having exactly two distinct factors. Since 17 meets this definition, (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: The length and breadth of a rectangle are in the ratio 3:2, and its perimeter is 50 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Half the perimeter = 25 cm = length + breadth = 3x + 2x = 5x, so x = 5. Length = 15, breadth = 10, and area = 15 × 10 = 150 sq cm. 120, 180 and 100 sq cm do not match these dimensions, so 150 sq cm is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: In a certain group of people, all who play chess also play carrom, and some who play carrom also play cards. Which conclusion definitely follows?
questions.explanation: The first premise directly states that everyone who plays chess also plays carrom, so 'all chess players play carrom' definitely follows. 'All carrom players play chess' reverses the statement, 'all card players play chess' is not supported, and 'no chess player plays cards' is not stated, so only the first conclusion follows.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Read the following data on the number of cars sold by a dealer over four months:

January → 40
February → 55
March → 35
April → 50

What is the average number of cars sold per month?
questions.explanation: The average is the total number of cars divided by the number of months: (40 + 55 + 35 + 50)/4 = 180/4 = 45 cars per month. The values 40, 50 and 48 do not equal 180 divided by 4, so they are incorrect, leaving 45 as the correct monthly average.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the data set: 6, 9, 9, 12, 14.

(i) The mean is 10.
(ii) The mode is 9.
(iii) The median is 9.
(iv) The range is 6.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Mean = (6+9+9+12+14)/5 = 50/5 = 10 (i); mode = 9 (ii); median (middle value) = 9 (iii). Statement (iv) is wrong because the range = 14 − 6 = 8, not 6, so any option containing (iv) is incorrect, leaving (i), (ii) and (iii).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A person saves 30% of his monthly salary. If he spends ₹14,000 in a month, what is his monthly salary?
questions.explanation: If he saves 30%, he spends 70% of his salary, and 70% = ₹14,000, so salary = 14,000 × 100/70 = ₹20,000. ₹18,000 would make spending ₹12,600, ₹22,000 gives ₹15,400 and ₹24,000 gives ₹16,800, none of which is ₹14,000, so ₹20,000 is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank in the number series: 100, 50, 25, 12.5, __________
questions.explanation: Each term is exactly half of the previous one: 100/2 = 50, 50/2 = 25, 25/2 = 12.5, so the next term is 12.5/2 = 6.25. The values 5, 10 and 6 are not exactly half of 12.5, so they do not fit the halving pattern, leaving 6.25 as the correct next term.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A dishonest trader claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a weight of 900 grams instead of 1 kilogram. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: He gives 900 g but charges for 1000 g, so his gain on cost = (100/900) × 100 ≈ 11.1%. A flat 10% wrongly takes the shortfall over 1000 g, about 9.1% divides incorrectly, and 12.5% overstates the gain, so about 11.1% is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: The ratio of the number of boys to girls in a class is 7:5. If there are 20 more boys than girls, how many students are there in the class?
questions.explanation: The difference in ratio parts is 7 − 5 = 2, which equals 20, so one part = 10. Total students = (7 + 5) × 10 = 120. 100, 144 and 108 do not fit a 7:5 ratio with a difference of 20, so 120 is correct.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: Which part of the computer is often referred to as the 'brain' of the computer?
questions.explanation: The Central Processing Unit (CPU) executes instructions and performs calculations, so it is called the brain of the computer. The hard disk stores data, the monitor displays output, and RAM holds data temporarily, but none of these performs the central processing role, so the CPU is correct.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about computer networks:

(i) LAN stands for Local Area Network.
(ii) A modem converts digital signals to analog and vice versa.
(iii) The Internet is an example of a WAN.
(iv) A router is used only to print documents.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: LAN means Local Area Network (i), a modem modulates and demodulates signals (ii), and the Internet is a Wide Area Network (iii). Statement (iv) is wrong because a router forwards data between networks, not for printing, so any option containing (iv) is incorrect.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: In MS Word, which shortcut key is commonly used to make selected text bold?
questions.explanation: Ctrl + B applies bold formatting to selected text. Ctrl + I applies italics, Ctrl + U applies underline, and Ctrl + D opens the font dialog box, so Ctrl + B is the correct shortcut for bold.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are examples of utility software?

(i) Antivirus program
(ii) Disk defragmenter
(iii) MS Excel
(iv) File compression tool

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Antivirus programs, disk defragmenters and file compression tools are utility software that help maintain and optimise the system (i, ii, iv). MS Excel (iii) is application software for a specific user task, not a utility, so any option containing (iii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: What is the full form of 'RAM' in computer terminology?
questions.explanation: RAM stands for Random Access Memory, a volatile memory that allows data to be read or written in any order. 'Read Access Memory', 'Rapid Access Memory' and 'Readily Available Memory' are not the correct expansions, so Random Access Memory is correct.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): It is safer to use a strong, unique password for each online account.
Reason (R): If one account is compromised, unique passwords prevent easy access to the others.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Using strong, unique passwords is safer, so (A) is correct, and unique passwords do stop attackers from reusing a leaked password on other accounts, so (R) is correct. Because this protection against reuse is exactly why unique passwords are safer, (R) correctly explains (A).

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: In an email address, what does the part after the '@' symbol usually represent?
questions.explanation: In an email address like name@example.com, the part after the '@' (example.com) identifies the domain or mail server that handles the account. It is not a password, subject line or attachment name, so the domain/mail server is the correct meaning.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Match the file extensions in Column I with the type of file in Column II:

Column I:
(a) .mp3
(b) .jpg
(c) .exe
(d) .txt

Column II:
(i) Image file
(ii) Executable program
(iii) Plain text file
(iv) Audio file

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: .mp3 is an audio file (iv), .jpg is an image file (i), .exe is an executable program (ii) and .txt is a plain text file (iii). The other options swap audio with image or interchange executable and text, giving wrong file types, so only the first mapping is correct.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The physical components of a computer that can be seen and touched are collectively called __________.
questions.explanation: Hardware refers to the tangible, physical parts of a computer such as the keyboard, monitor and CPU. Software is the set of programs, firmware is software stored on hardware chips, and malware is harmful software, none of which is the physical component, so 'hardware' is correct.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: Which of the following units is the largest measure of computer storage?
questions.explanation: In increasing order the units are kilobyte, megabyte, gigabyte and terabyte, so a terabyte is the largest of the four listed. A gigabyte is 1024 megabytes and a terabyte is 1024 gigabytes, making the terabyte the biggest, so it is correct.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a web browser?
questions.explanation: Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome and Safari are all web browsers used to access websites. Adobe Photoshop is an image-editing application, not a web browser, so it is the correct answer to the 'NOT a web browser' question.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about software and files:

(i) A PDF file can be read using a PDF reader.
(ii) An antivirus program helps detect and remove malware.
(iii) 'Save As' allows a file to be saved with a new name or format.
(iv) The Recycle Bin permanently deletes files immediately.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: A PDF reader opens PDF files (i), antivirus software detects and removes malware (ii), and 'Save As' saves a file under a new name or format (iii). Statement (iv) is wrong because the Recycle Bin temporarily holds deleted files and allows recovery, so any option with (iv) is incorrect.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: In MS Excel, what will the formula =AVERAGE(2, 4, 6, 8) return?
questions.explanation: The AVERAGE function adds the values and divides by their count: (2 + 4 + 6 + 8)/4 = 20/4 = 5. 20 is the sum, not the average, 8 is the largest value, and 4 is one of the numbers, so 5 is the correct result.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an input device that reads printed text or images into a computer?
questions.explanation: A scanner reads printed documents or images and converts them into digital form, so it is an input device. A printer and a monitor produce output, and a speaker outputs sound, so none of them reads printed material into the computer, making the scanner correct.

questions.subject: E
questions.questionText: What does the term 'booting' refer to in the context of computers?
options: Starting up the computer and loading the operating system
questions.correctAnswer: Starting up the computer and loading the operating system
questions.explanation: Booting is the process of starting a computer and loading the operating system into memory so it becomes ready to use. Shutting down is the reverse process, deleting temporary files is disk cleanup, and connecting to the internet is a separate task, so the start-up definition is correct.
